summary.headline: ISGEC Q2 FY27: standalone revenue up 17% to INR 1,457 crore, orders in hand at record INR 8,757 crore; consolidated orders INR 10,273 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations rose 17% YoY in Q2 to INR 1,457 crore and 35% in H1 to INR 3,010 crore, with PBT up 39% in the quarter. Management reported manufacturing EBIT margin of 13.7% (above its 12-13% guidance) and project EBIT margin of 5.7%, close to the 6% target. Consolidated PBT of INR 102 crore was driven down relative to standalone by losses from the Philippines ethanol plant (INR 164 crore loss in H1, including interest, depreciation and forex). Net borrowings fell sharply to INR 206 crore standalone and INR 156 crore consolidated as at September 30, 2026.

segments.name: Manufacturing (standalone)
segments.commentary: EBIT margin of 13.7% in Q2, above the 12-13% guided range. Management guides 12-13% for FY27.

segments.name: Projects (standalone)
segments.commentary: EBIT margin of 5.7% in Q2, close to the 6% target; guided to reach around 6% by year end.

segments.name: Isgec Hitachi Zosen (JV)
segments.commentary: Order book INR 1,161 crore at Sep 30, 2026, of which about INR 800 crore export; H1 orders INR 678 crore. FY27 turnover guided up 7-8% and profit up 5-7%.

segments.name: Saraswati Sugar Mills
segments.commentary: Revenue lower in the quarter due to lower cane availability last year and reduced sales quotas; cane supply this season expected only marginally above last season.

segments.name: Philippines ethanol (Cavite Biofuel / CBPI)
segments.commentary: H1 segment loss of INR 164 crore including interest; plant ran at 65-70% capacity on molasses, with a Q2 forex loss of INR 41 crore and a Q2 PBIT loss of about INR 60 crore. Plant under seasonal maintenance; restart expected December 2026.

guidance_outlook: Standalone FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15-17%; management indicated H2 revenue of roughly INR 3,200-3,300 crore versus H1 INR 3,010 crore.
Manufacturing EBIT margin guided at 12-13% for FY27; projects margin to improve to around 6% by year end.
Isgec Hitachi Zosen FY27 turnover expected up 7-8% and profit up 5-7% versus last year.

Philippines ethanol: Q3 expected weak with some profit from about 3 million litres of stock; Q4 (Jan-Mar 2027) targeted at about 90% utilisation; management gave no formal FY27 guidance but expects small positive EBITDA.
Depreciation at Cavite Biofuel expected at about INR 8-9 crore per quarter for Q3 and Q4 after the method change.

Capex expansion of about INR 500 crore expected to add about INR 1,200 crore of revenue, with less than INR 100 crore in FY27 and the bulk in FY28-FY29; management said a top-up of capex is possible but not firmed up.
capex_capacity: About INR 500-502 crore manufacturing capacity expansion, of which INR 199 crore spent cumulatively and funded from internal accruals.

New presses and machine-building plant at Bhartoli (Haryana); skids and modules facility in SEZ at Dahej (Gujarat); capacity and machining expansion at both casting factories; tube and piping shops at Rattangarh; standard mechanical presses factory at Bawal.
Projects are running largely on schedule; some new production facilities to be progressively completed during FY27.
Ethanol plant (Philippines) at 65-70% capacity during the season; sugarcane crushing ended April 20, 2026; restart expected December 2026 when new season starts.
demand_pricing: Standalone orders booked in H1 were INR 4,844 crore (management cited INR 4,400-plus crore in the Q&A); orders in hand at an all-time high of INR 8,757 crore standalone and INR 10,273 crore consolidated.
Products division share of consolidated order book is about 38%, versus the historical 25-28% range; orders come from automobile, oil and gas, petrochemicals, with small cement and steel orders.

Management says demand is robust across domestic and export markets; export inquiries from Latin America and Africa are healthy. Q2 export revenue INR 172 crore (about 11% of total income) versus INR 90 crore a year earlier.
Most product-division orders are fixed-price with no price variation clause; project orders are case-by-case with few price variation clauses.

Commodity prices (steel, copper, aluminium, nickel) moved up to 10% in the quarter and eased slightly in October; Middle East conflict is raising some material costs with a small adverse effect on profitability. Material cost is about 50-60% of manufactured product cost; back-to-back supplier offers and rate contracts are used to protect margins.
Management says a weaker rupee supports export competitiveness.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15-17% standalone FY27 revenue guidance conservative given H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 revenue of about INR 3,000 crore implies H2 of about INR 3,200-3,300 crore to hit guidance, with the bulk of new large orders converting in later years, moving the revenue run rate from about INR 5,200 crore to about INR 6,200 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Cavite Biofuel depreciation and loss outlook for Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation is INR 8 crore in Q2 and expected at INR 8-9 crore per quarter in Q3 and Q4 after a change in method; the Q2 loss includes forex. Q3 is expected to be weak but helped by sale of about 3 million litres of ethanol stock, and Q4 utilisation is targeted at around 90%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Isgec Hitachi Zosen in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Turnover is expected to rise about 7-8% and profit about 5-7% versus last year; order book is INR 1,161 crore, of which about INR 800 crore is export.

qa_highlights.question: What makes up standalone other income and what is the subsidiary-related component?
qa_highlights.answer: Management referred to slide 19 of the presentation, which splits subsidiary items into dividends (from Saraswati Sugar Mills and Isgec Hitachi Zosen), interest on loans to Isgec Investments Singapore and CBPI, forex on those loans, and an expected credit loss of INR 17 crore, offset by finance cost on bank borrowings on-lent to CBPI.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR 500 crore capex be topped up, and what revenue can it deliver by FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex is evaluated continually and a top-up is possible but not firmed up; the programme should add about INR 1,200 crore of revenue by FY29 at roughly 12-13% margin, and the products division could reach about INR 4,000 crore consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: How did the company protect margins through commodity volatility, and is 5.5% project margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a shift to shorter-cycle, technology-oriented projects with lower uncertainty and better cash flow; product orders are back-to-back hedged with suppliers and contingencies, and the company did not disclose specific raw-material changes.

risks_watch: Philippines ethanol losses: H1 loss of INR 164 crore, forex swings (INR 41 crore in Q2), and a weak Q3 before the December restart; depends on cane availability and the 90% Q4 utilisation target.
Commodity and freight volatility from Middle East conflict; management says most cost increases are absorbed by contingencies, but adverse margin impact is acknowledged.
Expansion execution: capex revenue benefit (INR 1,200 crore) is mostly in FY28-FY29, and management said projects are running largely on schedule without firm commitments on timing.
Largely fixed-price product orders leave limited pass-through of input cost rises.
Saraswati Sugar Mills volumes depend on weak cane availability; sugar realisation benefits are expected but volumes remain low.
Hitachi JV margin weakness in H1 (questioned by an analyst) with FY27 profit growth guided at only 5-7%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book and standalone margins, with specific numerical guidance. Noticeably more cautious and less specific on the Philippines ethanol business, where management declined to give FY27 guidance and corrected its own earlier utilisation comment. Evasive on product-wise revenue split and on the raw-material risk strategy.
key_quotes: Order booking for the six months is excellent at INR 4,844 crores, and standalone orders in hand as on September 30, 2026 are at an all-time high of INR 8,757 crores.
Current geopolitical developments have not affected order booking or order execution.
We are not going to take very long duration projects.
So I don't think we are in a situation to give out a guidance.
